sentence_stem: My hair was far too long, so
correct_completion: I had it cut at the salon.
full_sentence: My hair was far too long, so I had it cut at the salon.
acceptable_variants: I got it cut at the salon.
I booked an appointment with a hairdresser.

options.text: I did not care about my appearance.
options.why_wrong: 'So' introduces a sensible reaction to a problem, so indifference breaks the logical link.

options.text: I went to the gym for a workout.
options.why_wrong: This is unrelated to hair length, so it does not complete the cause-effect link.

options.text: I had it cut at the salon.
I asked my friend to tell me a joke.
options.why_wrong: This does not respond to the problem of long hair, so the cause-effect link is lost.

explanation: After 'so', we need a logical result of the first clause. The causative 'have + object + past participle' shows that the speaker arranges for someone else to perform the action, which is the key pattern here. Learners often confuse it with the active form, so compare 'I cut my hair' with 'I had my hair cut'.
translation: Moje włosy były zdecydowanie za długie, więc kazałem je obciąć w salonie.
